respuesta.razonamiento: The visual diagram presents Snapchat's snap submission and messaging architecture. The iOS and Android mobile clients interact with microservices hosted within an Amazon EKS cluster (Gateway, Media Delivery Service, Messaging Service MCS, Friend Graph, and SnapDB). External AWS persistence and caching services include CloudFront, S3, ElastiCache, and DynamoDB. The general 'AWS' platform container and mentioned 'Graviton' instance optimization are omitted as decorative/infrastructure layers. All 10 drawn lines match the narration workflow from snap upload to message delivery.
respuesta.nombre: Snapchat Media Delivery and Messaging Architecture on EKS

edges.notes: iOS app sends snap and message request via Gateway
edges.respaldo: line b0->b2; 'The first thing which happens is the iOS app uses our gateway'

edges.notes: Gateway routes request to Media Delivery Service
edges.respaldo: line b2->b3; 'to talk to the media delivery service'

edges.notes: Media Delivery Service sends media to CloudFront
edges.respaldo: line b3->b7; 'send the snap to CloudFront'

edges.notes: CloudFront persists media content in S3
edges.respaldo: line b7->b8; 'and purchase it in S3'

edges.notes: Media Delivery Service interacts with Friend Graph
Gateway forwards message details to MCS
Messaging Service writes message metadata to SnapDB
SnapDB stores data backed by DynamoDB
edges.respaldo: line b6->b10; 'SnapDB, which under the covers uses DynamoDB'

edges.notes: Messaging Service looks up recipient server/connection ID in ElastiCache
edges.respaldo: line b4->b9; 'the first thing the messaging service does is it looks up a connection ID, a server ID from ElastiCache'

edges.notes: Messaging Service pushes message over persistent connection to Android client
edges.respaldo: line b4->b1; 'persistent connection which a server has to the Android client'
